Understanding sources

Text verification: Text matches retained identified source editions; audit available.

Theological review: No external theological review recorded.

Source-type labels and reading sequences are editorial navigation. They do not confer ecclesiastical approval.

Scripture

Identify book, chapter, verses, translation, and numbering. Preview editions are reading aids distinct from the quoted author’s translation.

Conciliar definitions and canons

Keep the named council, precise definition or canon, date, and reception scope visible. A doctrinal definition and a disciplinary canon are distinct units.

Catechisms and confessions

Identify the issuing body or author, edition, and intended audience. Read a historical catechism in its own context; named Protestant confessions speak for their stated tradition.

Liturgical and prayer texts

Identify the service, edition, translator, speakers, and rubric boundaries. Published service selections are not newly written parish instructions.

Patristic commentary and theological works

Read the argument around a selection and identify its translator. An excerpt verifies an author’s words; it is not by itself a determination of universal reception.

Lives of saints and traditional accounts

Identify the narrator, date, genre, and source. Distinguish a received narrative or reported miracle from independently established historical detail.

Contemporary teaching and historical scholarship

Identify the speaker, jurisdiction where applicable, publication date, and source type. A recording, transcript, pastoral answer, and scholarly argument are different forms of evidence.

Terminology and language forms

Definitions link the original reading and its location. Pronunciation is included only when verified; this edition supplies no generated phonetics or synthetic pronunciation.
